clusters.name: Walter's move across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move with the family from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952, within the year: June grew anxious and homesick, writing to her sister Edna every day; Walter spent long hours out in the trees and grew distant from June; Glen began fighting at his new school; Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; Walter and June rowed over money for new trees; by September, June had joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out, her anxiety easing. These shifts pile up in the months after the move, each touching on the family's adjustment to the new place and the strains it brought between Walter and June, and in Glen at school.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968, when the late frost destroyed the crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter began drinking heavily most nights; he and Glen blamed each other for the loan and fell into conflict; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and the talks with the bank; Glen's asthma attacks worsened that winter; you began wetting the bed again in April 1969; Ida developed heart trouble and was told to stop working at the bakery; by October 1969, Walter had stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees. The shifts gather in the months around the loss of the orchard and the family's move to Ridgeport, each one touching on the strain between Walter and Glen, the weight on Glen's shoulders, and the trouble it brought to those close to them.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's loss of his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the following year: Glen was out of work most of that year and sat in the truck in the yard for hours; he and Marian fought loudly at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; you kept to your room and grew distant from your mother; Walter began drinking again after six years off it; by June 1976, after Glen began driving a delivery truck for the feed store in March, you were eating again and made the track team. The shifts gather in the months after Glen lost his work, each one touching on the strain between Glen and Marian, the weight on Marian's shoulders, and the trouble it brought to you and to Walter.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving into your house in January 1990, after she sold her farm: you clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals; you worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows; Hollis took his mother's side; Owen began having tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice; Wilma took over Lily's care; you developed eczema flaring on both hands; you and Hollis rowed most nights; by June 1991, when Wilma took a flat in town, your eczema had cleared over the summer. The shifts gather in the months after Wilma's arrival, with conflict between you and her, Hollis caught between his wife and his mother, Owen showing trouble at school, and your own symptoms flaring and then easing as the household settled into a new balance.
